correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=4 the closed-neighborhood condition reduces exactly to two layer-sum inequalities. All cases are partitioned by existence of low labels on either clique. The light/light case has only layer totals 3 or4 and is counted exhaustively by four allowed ordered pairs; both mixed cases are conditioned on light weight 0,1,2; high/high labels are unrestricted. Disjoint cases give every coefficient. A direct graph-neighborhood C++ checker exhausts 4^(2n) assignments for n<=6, and an independently formulated exact 16-state layer-total convolution matches the formula through n=9. The arbitrary-n proof does not rely on finite checks.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact weight enumerator for a natural infinite vertex-transitive graph family rather than a relabeling of the known scalar domination minimum. It reveals a sharp change at n=4 versus weaker Roman {3}, the motivated optimizer count C(n,3)^2+n^3, and two linearly growing forbidden-weight intervals for n>=5. The light/heavy structural dichotomy explains why the spectrum is split into three full bands, yielding nontrivial support information useful to related defense-enumerator and graph-product studies.
